similar_scenes.name: Brit-pop y post-pop
similar_scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
similar_scenes.desc: Como tantas veces, el fenómeno más publicitado es el menos interesante: un «brit-pop» de grupos terriblemente parecidos y tediosos, sin apenas imaginación. Lo anticipan Lightning Seeds, La's, Teenage Fanclub y Heavenly; estalla con Boo Radleys, Blur (Parklife) y Oasis (el «farol» que mejor personifica la moda). Suede y el glam-pop (Super Furry Animals, Placebo), las excepciones de High Llamas (Hawaii) y Supergrass, el revival mod (Ocean Colour Scene, Wildhearts), Elastica, Sleeper, las Spice Girls; Trembling Blue Stars, Tindersticks, Delgados. El post-pop de Radiohead, «la banda más publicitada y sobrevalorada de la década», cuyo OK Computer es una obra maestra del falso vanguardismo; Coldplay, Travis.

podcast.title: Movement Decline (1996-1997)
podcast.body: The Brit-Pop movement began to decline around 1996-1997, with its sound "making water" as public interest shifted to other things. Bands like Pulp and Blur were notable for successfully escaping the movement and not getting "stuck" in its dying sound. "the Brit-Pop movement was falling apart, people were already talking about other things."

podcast.title: British Scene in the 1990s
podcast.body: Brit Pop was a significant musical movement in Britain during the 1990s, often associated with the Manchester scene. "while Britain has a great time with Manchester and Brit Pop."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Early Spark
podcast.body: The Brit-pop movement likely began around 1989, with Suede often considered its vanguard. "Justo en 1989 casi a la vez arrancaba el movimiento Britop posiblemente con sweat, que era un poco la avanza dilla."

srcs.episode: La generación perdida del Indie: SHOEGAZE

podcast.title: Golden Age and Pillars
podcast.body: The mid-1990s are described as a "golden age" for Brit-Pop as a record label movement, characterized by four main "pillars" or leading bands, of which Pulp was one. "this small special on that golden age of Brit-Pop, of Brit-Pop as a record movement and these four small specials of the four pillars of Brit-Pop."

podcast.title: Gorillaz Debut Album Component
podcast.body: Brit-pop elements were incorporated into the experimental musical blend of the Gorillaz's debut album. "The music was rather experimental, more trip-hop, some alt-rock, bits of Brit-pop, little dub, little reggae, and a bunch of hip-hop."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Immediate Label Support
podcast.body: From its very beginning, Brit-pop benefited from immediate record label support, including massive production and distribution within months of its appearance, a stark contrast to the challenges faced by Shoegaze. "De haber tenido el apoyo discográfico que al mejor tuvieron desde un inicio el Britpop."

srcs.episode: La generación perdida del Indie: SHOEGAZE

podcast.title: Oasis at the Forefront (1990s)
podcast.body: Oasis was a leading figure in the Brit Pop movement throughout the 1990s, defining its sound and enjoying immense popularity with their "edgy brand." "On stage, they're edgy brand of Brit Pop, one of the millions of fans."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The 100 Greatest Rock Moments of the Millennium So Far - Part 8: (30-21)

podcast.title: Oasis's 90s Imperial Era
podcast.body: The 90s career of the Brit pop band Oasis is referenced as an example where the term "imperial phase" is used, even in discussions about its tail end or "crash." "looking back on the 90s career of the Brit pop band Oasis featuring host Yasi Salik and her guest Rob Harvilla. Oasis is still in their imperial phase."

srcs.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia

podcast.title: Rebirth as Indy Rock
podcast.body: After Brit Pop became "tired," it was reborn under the guise of Indy Rock in the late 1990s and early 2000s. "But that gets tired after a while but is reborn under the guise of Indy Rock in the late 90s and early 2000s."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Revolution and Industry Shift
podcast.body: By 1991, young bands like Blur and Oasis were revolutionizing British pop, causing the recording industry to reorient its focus towards this new generation, leaving the previously struggling Shoegaze generation behind. "ya en 1991 unos jovencísimos Blood y Basis revolucionaban el pobre tánico, y ya digamos que la industria discográfica se orientaba hacia otro lugar."

podcast.title: Second Indie Generation Cornerstone
podcast.body: Brit-Pop emerged in the United Kingdom between 1989 and 1993, representing one of the two major movements that defined modern indie music, alongside Grunge in the US. "por el otro lado sería el Brit-Pop en el Reino Unido."
